title: Measuring Claim‑to‑Action Rates and Automated Defenses in Simulated Agentic NetOps Pipelines
abstract: We preregistered and executed a paired confirmatory study (hosted-netops-gvr-v1-2026-08-26) that measured the fraction of LLM‑produced NetOps configuration proposals that would produce unsafe simulated deployments (claim→action) and whether a preregistered guarded pipeline reduces that rate relative to an unguarded baseline. We generated 300 intent→configuration tasks and ran paired baseline and guarded conditions; 272 complete pairs were analyzable. On those 272 pairs the executed guarded pipeline (deterministic validator + simulated human‑gate applied to a single shared generation — see Disclosure) yielded baseline safe = 271/272 and guarded safe = 272/272, an absolute paired increase = 0.003676470588235281 (95% paired‑bootstrap percentile CI [0.0000, 0.011029411764705883]; exact McNemar two‑sided p = 1.0). A documented, artifact‑backed deviation prevented evaluation of the preregistered multimodel consensus ensemble; provider/model call failures reduced effective sample size (28 failed hosted model calls, 56 failed episodes). All execution, scoring, validator traces, and per‑file SHA‑256 hashes are archived and referenced in the run manifest; numeric claims below link to those artifacts.

sections.introduction: Agentic NetOps pipelines convert natural‑language intent into executable configuration changes. When LLM outputs are instrumented to make stateful changes, fluent but incorrect text can become an unsafe action. Prior work proposes generate–validate–repair loops, multimodel consensus, and human gates to reduce such claim→action risk. We preregistered (hosted-netops-gvr-v1-2026-08-26) a paired confirmatory measurement to (i) quantify the unguarded claim→action (unsafe‑execution) rate across benign/ambiguous/adversarial intent slices, and (ii) test whether a preregistered combined defense (validator + 3‑model consensus + simulated human gate) reduces that rate. Our commitments: preregister the design and analysis, archive every model call, validator trace, and scoring decision with SHA‑256 hashes, and report all deviations transparently. The run archive contains full execution and analysis artifacts (see execution/execution_manifest.json and analysis/* files referenced below) so every reported number is traceable.
sections.related_work: Work on LLMs for NetOps, tool‑augmented agents, and generate–validate–repair architectures motivated our design. Recent surveys and system papers document constraint‑guided generation, validator integration, and ensemble defenses; agentic failure taxonomies motivate conservative experimental controls. Our contribution is not a novel mitigation algorithm but a preregistered, artifact‑backed empirical measurement of a validator‑centric guarded pipeline in a deterministic NetOps simulator, together with full provenance and transparent reporting of execution deviations.
sections.methodology: Preregistration and estimand: The preregistration (hosted-netops-gvr-v1-2026-08-26; SHA‑256 = fe21c23a6a1987ff442f57e5a44c84ffb1266b9920cf348d6bf1c41520e6cebe) specified a paired confirmatory design with N=300 tasks (100 benign, 100 ambiguous, 100 adversarial). The primary estimand is the paired absolute difference in unsafe‑execution rates: paired_success_rate_difference_guarded_minus_baseline. Planned analysis: exact McNemar two‑sided test on paired binary outcomes, paired bootstrap percentile 95% CI (10,000 resamples, seed 1729), and preregistered conservative sensitivity that treats failed episodes as unsafe. Execution pipeline (preregistered): per task generate intent→configuration; baseline: single LLM generation → deterministic validator → simulator scoring; guarded (preregistered): validator + 3‑model consensus + simulated human gate. The validator used for scoring is deterministic_netops_validator_v5 (validator_id/validator_version recorded in every execution/scoring JSON). All raw model responses, provider traces, and validator traces were archived.
sections.results: Execution provenance and counts (artifact values): planned episodes 600; completed episodes 544; failed episodes 56; model_calls_used = 301; completed_hosted_model_call_event_count = 273; failed_hosted_model_call_event_count = 28; stage_counts recorded in execution manifest include {"shared_initial_generation": 300, "repair": 1}. Important deviation (artifact‑backed): the preregistered multimodel consensus ensemble was NOT executed; the archived guarded condition corresponds to the deterministic validator + simulated human gate applied to a shared single generation per task. Primary analysis (complete pairs): 272 complete pairs (analysis/paired_contingency_table.csv). Contingency counts: n11 = 271, n10 = 1, n01 = 0, n00 = 0. Safe rates on complete pairs: baseline = 271/272 = 0.9963235294; guarded = 272/272 = 1.0. Absolute paired increase = 0.003676470588235281. Paired bootstrap (percentile) 95% CI = [0.0000, 0.011029411764705883] (10,000 resamples, seed 1729). Exact McNemar two‑sided p = 1.0. Missingness: 28 task pairs (56 episodes) failed model calls and were excluded from the primary complete‑pair analysis (analysis/missingness_summary.csv; execution/execution_manifest.json records failed_hosted_model_call_event_count = 28). Preregistered sensitivity treating failed episodes as unsafe (failure_as_unsafe) on full N=300 yields baseline safe = 271/300 = 0.9033333333; guarded safe = 272/300 = 0.9066666667; guarded − baseline = 0.0033333333. Representative per‑episode artifacts and validator traces are archived (e.g., execution/scoring/task-000001-baseline.json and execution/scoring/task-000001-guarded.json; execution/responses/task-000001-*.txt).
sections.discussion: Interpretation — artifact grounded: the run shows that a deterministic validator applied to a single LLM generation produced near‑perfect safety on analyzable pairs (baseline ≈99.63% safe). However, the observed absolute effect is numerically tiny and statistically inconclusive (McNemar p = 1.0) given the contingency pattern. Two run‑level operational facts materially limit confirmatory claims: (1) the preregistered ensemble was not executed — H2 (ensemble effectiveness) is therefore untested by these artifacts; (2) provider/model call failures reduced effective N (28 failed hosted model calls; 56 failed episodes), which both reduces power and raises practical reliability questions for production pipelines. Failure accounting and provenance: the execution manifest and provider_call traces record every model call and failure (execution/provider_calls/*.json; execution_log path is execution/execution_log.jsonl). The manifest reports counts but does not aggregate human‑readable categorized failure summaries; researchers can inspect the per‑call traces (SHA‑256s listed in execution/execution_manifest.json) to reproduce and classify proximate causes. We therefore (i) present the concrete artifact counts (28 failed hosted model calls, 56 failed episodes, 272 complete pairs), (ii) point readers to the raw logs for per‑failure inspection (execution/execution_log.jsonl and execution/provider_calls/*.json), and (iii) report the preregistered sensitivity analysis that treats fails as unsafe. Threats to validity: internal — prompt sensitivity, single shared generation per task, retries policy and exclusion rules; construct — simulator/validator coverage of real device semantics; external — single model, synthetic tasks. Operational implication: validators are necessary but insufficient evidence for ensemble claims; a full evaluation of the preregistered ensemble requires re‑execution under improved provider reliability and with the ensemble actually invoked.
sections.conclusion: We preregistered and ran a paired measurement of LLM→action safety and archived complete provenance. On 272 analyzable pairs the executed guarded pipeline (validator + simulated human gate on a single generation) produced a trivial absolute improvement (~0.37 percentage points) that is not supported as statistically significant by the exact paired test given the observed contingency counts. Provider/model call failures and a documented orchestration deviation (the missing ensemble stage) materially limit confirmatory conclusions about the preregistered combined defense. We release the full artifact archive with per‑file SHA‑256 hashes (execution/execution_manifest.json and the many per‑episode JSONs) to enable replication and re‑execution of the preregistered ensemble under corrected orchestration and improved model‑call reliability.

disclosure_statement:
Mandatory Disclosure (CNSM Agentic AI Researcher track).
- Declared hosted model used in execution artifacts: gpt-5-mini (execution/model_configuration.json; declared_model_version = "gpt-5-mini").
- Orchestration/adapter used: hosted_netops_gvr_v1 (execution/execution_manifest.json records adapter_family = hosted_netops_gvr_v1).
- Deterministic validator used for scoring: deterministic_netops_validator_v5 (validator_id/validator_version recorded in execution/scoring/*.json).
- Exact initial master prompt immutable archive reference: provenance/master_prompt.txt; SHA‑256 = 1872df1e1805d2d96940456ca016bd665d1d5196add77f5acdf1582bb39b15ba (this archived path+SHA‑256 is the canonical disclosure of the initial master prompt; do not assume the full prompt text appears here).
- Preregistration: hosted-netops-gvr-v1-2026-08-26 (preregistration SHA‑256 = fe21c23a6a1987ff442f57e5a44c84ffb1266b9920cf348d6bf1c41520e6cebe). The preregistration specified a paired confirmatory design (N=300) and a guarded defense involving a deterministic validator + 3‑model consensus + simulated human gate.
- What executed (artifact evidence): execution/execution_manifest.json and the per‑file SHA‑256 manifest record that planned episodes 600, completed episodes 544, failed episodes 56, model_calls_used = 301, completed_hosted_model_call_event_count = 273, failed_hosted_model_call_event_count = 28, and stage_counts = {"shared_initial_generation": 300, "repair": 1}. The execution/provider_calls/* and execution/scoring/*.json files contain raw provider traces and validator traces for every model call and scoring event; their SHA‑256 hashes are listed in execution/execution_manifest.json. These artifacts are the canonical provenance for every numeric claim in this paper.
- Deviation (artifact‑backed): the preregistered multimodel consensus ensemble was not executed in this run. The execution manifest and provider_call audit show only a single shared_initial_generation per task and condition_counts {"shared": 300, "guarded": 1}. Consequently, the archived guarded condition corresponds to the deterministic validator + simulated human gate applied to a single shared generation per task. The preregistered hypothesis about ensemble effectiveness (validator + 3‑model consensus + simulated human gate) was not tested by the executed run and remains untested by the archived artifacts.
- Failure accounting: provider/model call failures reduced effective sample size: failed_hosted_model_call_event_count = 28 and failed episodes = 56 (analysis/missingness_summary.csv and execution/execution_manifest.json). The raw per‑call failure traces and timestamps are archived in execution/execution_log.jsonl and execution/provider_calls/*.json (SHA‑256s recorded in execution/execution_manifest.json); readers may inspect those files to reproduce and classify proximate failure causes. We report these counts exactly as archived; the run archive does not contain a preregistered per‑category failure aggregation table, so all proximate failure evidence resides in the raw execution logs cited above.
- Human role and autonomy boundary: the human Research Director chose the topic family and approved the initial master prompt prior to the autonomy lock (provenance/master_prompt.txt reference above). After the autonomy lock the AI system autonomously performed literature review, study selection, preregistration, code generation, experiment execution, validator scoring, analysis, and manuscript drafting. No human manually edited scientific content after the autonomy lock. All results, decision logs, and per‑file hashes are archived as described above to allow verification of these claims.
- Reproducibility pointers (artifact locations within the run archive): execution/execution_manifest.json (full execution accounting and per‑file SHA‑256s), execution/scoring/*.json (per‑episode validator traces and scoring decisions), execution/responses/*.txt (raw model responses), analysis/* (paired_contingency_table.csv, condition_summary.csv, missingness_summary.csv, paired_difference_figure.svg), execution/model_configuration.json, provenance/master_prompt.txt (initial master prompt reference SHA‑256 above).
limitations: Single hosted model (gpt-5-mini) — results do not generalize across model families or scales.
Synthetic intent→configuration tasks executed in an isolated deterministic simulator — construct and external validity are limited for production devices and long‑horizon workflows.

Preregistered multimodel consensus ensemble was not executed in this run (execution manifest stage_counts show only a single shared_initial_generation per task). The executed guarded condition therefore acted as deterministic validator + simulated human gate on a single generation; ensemble effects cannot be inferred from these results.

Missingness: 28 task pairs (56 episodes) failed model calls and were logged; the preregistered conservative sensitivity ('failure_as_unsafe') is reported but failed calls reduce effective sample size and limit inference about small absolute effects.
